sections.content: Ayo describes founder hires as differentially higher-output, but also differentially higher-attrition. answer.summary: Omojola says founder-dense teams can produce more, but they also expose organizational waste and tend to have higher attrition; he also sees a positive effect on the wider team.

sections.heading: Tradeoffs
sections.content: At Carbon, Omojola says he hired founders for about 15% of the team over time; the team was about half founders when discussing its makeup. Founders quickly spot and call out waste or “bullshit,” which can mean a manager has to listen to pointed criticism. They are ambitious and often move on after roughly two to two-and-a-half years to lead elsewhere or start another company. He characterizes the result as a team with differentially higher output, but also differentially higher attrition.

sections.heading: Upside for the team
sections.content: Despite those costs, Omojola says he unequivocally loves having founders on the team. He also observed that a founder-dense team can level up its colleagues, and that people on such teams liked the environment; at Carbon, founders were present across multiple functions.
